Surah 13 is Medinan, though it is also said to be Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} He, the Exalted, informs that this Qur'an is the verses of the Book, which indicate everything that the servants need of the foundations of the religion (usul al-din) and its branches (furu'). And that what has been sent down to the Messenger from his Lord is the truth, the clear (al-Haqq al-Mubin), because its reports are true and its commands and prohibitions are just, supported by evidence and decisive proofs. So whoever turns towards it and towards its knowledge will be among the people of knowledge of the truth, which knowledge obliges them to act by what Allah loves. {But most of the people [do not believe]}: in this Qur'an, either out of ignorance, turning away from it, and lack of concern for it, or out of obstinacy and wrongdoing. Therefore most people do not benefit from it, due to the lack of the cause that necessitates benefit.

{2} He, may He be exalted, informs of His sole creation, management, greatness and sovereignty, which indicate that He alone is the One worthy of worship, and that worship is due to none but Him. He said: {Allah is He who raised the heavens} — in their immensity and vastness — by His great power, {without pillars that you can see}; that is, there are no pillars beneath them. For if there were pillars, you would see them. {Then} — after He created the heavens and the earth — {He established Himself upon the Throne}, the great one, which is the highest of the creations, in a manner befitting His majesty and suitable to His perfection. {And He subjected the sun and the moon} for the benefit of the servants and the benefit of their livestock and their fruits. {Each} of the sun and the moon {runs} by the management of the Mighty, the All-Knowing {until an appointed term}: moving in a regular course that neither slackens nor tires, until the appointed term arrives, which is the folding up by Allah of this world and the transfer of its people to the Hereafter, the abode of permanence. At that time Allah will fold up the heavens and replace them, and will alter the earth and replace it. The sun and the moon will be wound up and [brought together], and they will be cast into the Fire, so that whoever worshipped them will see that they were not deserving of worship, and he will be struck with the most intense regret; and so that those who disbelieved will know that they were liars. As for His saying: {He manages the affair, detailing the signs}: this combines creation and command. That is, Allah, the Mighty, has established Himself upon the throne of dominion, managing the affairs of the upper and lower worlds: He creates and provides, enriches and impoverishes, raises some peoples and lowers others, grants honor and humiliation, lowers and raises, pardons slips, relieves distresses, executes decrees at their appointed times, which His knowledge has preceded and His pen has recorded, sends forth His noble angels to carry out what He has appointed them to manage, sends down the divine Books upon His messengers, and clarifies what the servants need of laws, commands and prohibitions, detailing them to the utmost degree through their explanation, clarification and differentiation. {So that you} — through what He has shown you of signs in the horizons and the signs of the Qur'an — {may be certain of meeting your Lord}. For the abundance of proofs, their clarity and their evidence are among the causes of attaining certainty in all divine matters, especially in the great articles of faith, such as the Resurrection, the Gathering and the bringing forth from the graves.

Moreover, it is known that Allah is All-Wise; He does not create creatures in vain, nor leave them aimlessly. Just as He sent His messengers and revealed His Books for the command and prohibition of the servants, He must bring them to an abode in which His recompense will be realized for them; He will reward the good-doers with the best reward and recompense the evil-doers for their evil.

{3} {And it is He who spread out the earth}: that is, He created it for the servants, made it vast, blessed it, laid it out for the servants, and deposited in it what benefits them. {And placed in it firm mountains}: that is, great mountains, lest it sway with its creatures; for were it not for the mountains, it would shake with its inhabitants, since it rests upon a flow of water and has no stability or steadiness except through the firm mountains which Allah made as stakes for it. {And} He placed in it {rivers} that water the children of Adam, their animals and their crops; by them He brings forth from the trees, crops and fruits abundant good. Hence He said: {And of all the fruits He made in it two kinds, two}: that is, two varieties of what the servants need. {He covers the night over the day}: so the horizons are darkened, every creature settles into its resting place, and they rest from the fatigue and toil of the day. Then, when they have fulfilled their needs of sleep, the day covers the night, and behold, they are awake [dispersed] in their affairs and works during the day. {And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will give thanks}. {Surely in that are signs} regarding the divine purposes {for a people who reflect}: upon them, and look at them with the gaze of contemplation, indicating that He who created them, arranged them and directed them is Allah, there is no god but He and no one worthy of worship besides Him; that He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Compassionate, the Merciful; that He is capable of all things, Wise in all things, praised for what He created and commanded, blessed and exalted.

{4} {And} among the signs of His complete power and wondrous craftsmanship is that He made {in the earth adjoining tracts, and gardens}, containing various kinds of trees: vines, palm trees, crops and others; and palm trees, some of which are {clustered} — that is, several trees growing from one root — {and some not clustered}, each tree standing on its own. All are {watered with one water}, and their soil is one. {And We make some of them excel others in fruit}: in color, taste, benefit and delightfulness. Here is good land that produces abundant herbage, grass, trees and crops; here is land adjacent to it that produces no herbage and retains no water; here is land that retains water but produces no herbage; here is land that produces crops and trees but no herbage; here is fruit that is sweet, and here is fruit that is bitter, and here is what lies between. So is this diversity in their essence and nature, or is it the decree of the Mighty, the Merciful? {Surely in that are signs for a people who understand}: that is, for a people who possess intellects that guide them to what benefits them and lead them to what is right, and who understand from Allah His counsels, commands and prohibitions. As for those who turn away and the dull-witted, they wander in their darkness and hesitate in their error; they are not guided to their Lord by any path, nor do they heed His word.

{5} It is possible that the meaning of His saying: {And if you wonder} is: at the greatness of God Most High and the abundance of the proofs of Tawhid (monotheism). For wonder here is at the denial of the deniers and their rejection of the Resurrection, and their saying: {When we are dust, shall we indeed be [returned] in a new creation?}; that is: this is, in their estimation, extremely impossible, that after they have become dust, God would restore them. For out of their ignorance they measured the power of the Creator by the power of the created. So when they saw this to be impossible for the power of the created, they thought it was impossible for the power of the Creator, and they forgot that God created them the first time when they were nothing. It may also be that its meaning is: And if you wonder at their saying and their rejection of the Resurrection, then that is among the wonders. For the one to whom the signs are made clear, and who sees in them decisive proofs of the Resurrection beyond any doubt or suspicion, and then denies it, his saying is among the wonders. But this is not surprising from {those who disbelieved in their Lord}: that is, they denied His oneness, and it is the most manifest and evident of things. {Those are the shackles}: which prevent them from guidance {around their necks}: since they were called to faith and did not believe, and guidance was presented to them and they were not guided. So their hearts and minds were turned, as a punishment for their not believing in Him the first time. {Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally}: they will never come out of it.

{6} He, exalted is He, informs of the ignorance of those who denied His Messenger, the polytheists who associated others with Him, who were admonished but did not take heed, and for whom proofs were established but who did not submit to them. Rather, they openly denied, and they took the forbearance of Allah, the One, the Subduer, toward them, and His not hastening their punishment for their sins, as evidence that they were upon the truth. They kept urging the Messenger to bring the punishment, and one of them would say: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾! ﴿And [while] there have already passed away before them the exemplary punishments﴾; that is, the events and days of Allah concerning the nations who denied [their messengers]. Will they not then reflect upon their own condition and abandon their ignorance?! ﴿And indeed, your Lord is Forgiving to mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾; that is, His goodness, kindness, benevolence and pardon continue to descend upon the servants, while their polytheism and disobedience continue to ascend to Him. They disobey Him, and He calls them to His door; they commit crimes, and His goodness and kindness do not deprive them. If they repent to Him, then He is their Beloved, for He loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves. And if they do not repent, then He is their Physician: He tests them with calamities to purify them from their defects. ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ against whoever persists in sins, refusing repentance, seeking forgiveness, and turning to the Mighty, the Forgiving. So let the servants beware of His punishments inflicted upon the people of crimes, for His seizing is painful and severe.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 13, verse 7:

{7} That is: the disbelievers propose to you signs of their own choosing, and they say: ﴿Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ They make this statement of theirs an excuse for not responding to the Messenger, when in fact he is only a warner, having no part in the affair. Allah is the One who sends down the signs, and He has supported him with clear proofs that are not hidden from people of understanding, and by them whoever seeks the truth is guided. As for the disbeliever who, out of his wrongdoing and ignorance, proposes signs to Allah, this proposal of his is false, a lie and a fabrication; for if any sign at all had come to him, he would not have believed or submitted, because he has not refrained from belief for lack of anything indicating its truth, but only out of the desires of his soul and his pursuit of his appetites. ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾; that is, a caller who calls them to guidance from among the messengers and their followers, and with them are the proofs and evidences that indicate the soundness of the guidance they bring.

{8–9} He, exalted is He, informs of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, the breadth of His awareness, and His encompassing of everything. He says: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears﴾ — of the children of Adam and others — ﴿and what the wombs diminish and what they increase.﴾ That is: what the wombs lose of what they contain, whether the fetus perishes, shrinks, or is wasted away; and ﴿what they increase﴾: the wombs and the fetuses within them that grow larger. ﴿And everything with Him is in measure﴾: nothing precedes it or delays it, nor does it increase or decrease except as His wisdom and knowledge require. Indeed, He is ﴿the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted﴾: great in His essence, names, and attributes, ﴿the Exalted﴾ above all His creation by His essence, power, and dominance.

{10} ﴿Alike among you﴾ in His knowledge, hearing, and sight: ﴿whoever conceals speech and whoever publicizes it, and whoever is hidden by night and goes freely by day﴾ — that is, one who is settled in a concealed place within it, and ﴿goes freely by day﴾: one who is inside his hiding place during the day. The *sarab* (hiding place) is that in which a person conceals himself: either the inside of his house, a cave, a grotto, or the like.

{11} ﴿For him﴾ — that is, for the human being — ﴿are successive angels﴾ from among the angels who follow one another by night and by day, ﴿before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah﴾: they guard his body and soul from everyone who intends him harm, and they record his deeds for him. They are constantly attending him. Just as Allah's knowledge encompasses him, Allah has sent these guardians over the servants such that their states, their deeds, and nothing of them is hidden or forgotten. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change what is in a people﴾ of blessing, goodness, and abundant living, ﴿until they change what is in themselves﴾: by moving from faith to disbelief, from obedience to disobedience, or from thankfulness for Allah's blessings to insolence with them. Then Allah takes these blessings away from them at that point. Likewise, when the servants change what is in themselves of disobedience and turn to obedience of Allah, Allah changes what they were in of wretchedness into goodness, joy, happiness, and mercy. ﴿And when Allah intends for a people an evil﴾ — that is, punishment, hardship, or a matter they dislike — His will must take effect upon them, for ﴿there is no repeal of it﴾, and no one can prevent it from them, ﴿and they have no protector other than Him﴾ who manages their affairs, bringing them what is loved and repelling what is disliked. So let them beware of persisting in what Allah dislikes, lest there befall them a punishment that is not averted from the criminal people.

Therefore He said:

{14} That is, to Allah alone belongs {the call of truth}: it is His worship alone, with no partner, and sincerity in both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request directed to Him, may He be exalted. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 13, verse 15:

{15} That is: all that the heavens and the earth contain is submissive to its Lord, prostrating to Him ﴿willingly and unwillingly﴾. The willing submission belongs to those who come to prostration and humility by choice, like the believers, while the unwilling belongs to those who are too proud to worship their Lord, whose state and natural disposition (fitrah) contradict them in that. ﴿And their shadows, at morning and evening﴾; that is, the shadows of created things also prostrate to Him at the beginning and end of the day, and each thing's prostration is according to its state, as the Most High said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts [Allah] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾. So when all created things prostrate to their Lord, willingly and unwillingly, He is truly the God, the truly worshipped and truly praised, and the divinity of anything else is false. For this reason He mentioned its falsehood and proved it with His saying:

Say (to them, O Muhammad): Those who associate with Him idols and rivals, whom they love as they love Allah, and to whom they offer various forms of devotion and worship: Has your reason been so led astray that you have taken, besides Him, protectors whom you worship and to whom you give allegiance, though they are not deserving of that? For they ﴿do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm﴾. Yet you abandon the allegiance of Him who possesses the perfect names and attributes, who owns the living and the dead, in whose hand is creation, management, benefit and harm. Thus the worship of Allah alone and the worship of those who associate partners with Him are not equal, just as the blind and the seeing are not equal, and just as ﴿the darknesses and the light are not alike﴾. If they have doubt and confusion, and have made for Him partners, claiming that they created as He created and acted as He acts, then remove from them this confusion and ambiguity with the proof that indicates the oneness of God in unity. Say to them: Allah is the Creator of everything. It is impossible that anything should create itself, and it is equally impossible that anything should come into existence without a creator. Therefore it is established that there is a God, a Creator, who has no partner in His creation, because He is the One, the Irresistible (al-Wahid al-Qahhar). Oneness and irresistible dominion exist only for Allah alone. Every created thing is subject to a creature above it that dominates it, and above that dominator is a higher dominator, until dominion ends with the One, the Irresistible. Thus domination and unity are inseparably and necessarily God's alone. Thereby it is made clear, by the compelling rational proof, that what is invoked besides Allah has no share whatsoever in the creation of creatures, and on that basis its worship is void.

{17} The Exalted has likened the guidance that He sent down upon His Messenger to the life of hearts and spirits, to the water that He sent down for the life of bodies. He has likened the abundant general benefit of the guidance, which people are in dire need of, to the general and necessary benefit of rain. He has likened the hearts that carry the guidance, and their varying capacities, to the valleys through which torrents flow: a large valley holds a great deal of water, just as a large heart holds much knowledge, and a small valley takes in a little water, just as a small heart holds little knowledge... and so on. He has likened what arises in the hearts of desires and doubts when the truth reaches them to the scum that rises upon the water, and to the scum that rises upon the metal ore which is placed over fire in order to be purified and smelted. This scum keeps floating on the water, clouding it, until it departs and vanishes, leaving behind what benefits people: clear water and pure metal. Likewise, doubts and desires: the heart continues to hate them and to struggle against them with true proofs and firm resolve, until they depart and vanish, and the heart remains pure and clear, containing nothing but what benefits people, namely knowledge of the truth, preference for it, and desire for it. Thus falsehood departs, and the truth erases it: ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to perish﴾. He said here: ﴿Thus does Allah strike the examples﴾, meaning: so that the truth may be made clear from falsehood, and guidance from error.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 13, verse 18:

{18} When Allah, Exalted is He, made clear the truth from falsehood, He mentioned that people are of two categories: one who responds to his Lord, for whom He mentioned His reward, and one who does not respond, for whom He mentioned His punishment. He said: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord, there is the best (reward)﴾. That is: their hearts submitted to knowledge and faith, their limbs submitted to the commands and prohibitions, and they became in agreement with their Lord in what He wills from them. For them is ﴿the best﴾, that is: the good state and the good reward. For them are the most noble of attributes and the best of virtues, and of reward, both immediate and deferred, that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being. ﴿And as for those who did not respond to Him﴾, after He had set forth the parables for them and made the truth clear to them, for them is the state that is not good. So ﴿even if they had all that is on the earth entirely﴾: of gold, silver and other things, ﴿and the like of it with it﴾, ﴿they would ransom themselves with it﴾ from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection; it would not be accepted from them. And how could they have that? ﴿For them is the evil reckoning﴾: it is the reckoning that encompasses every evil deed they committed and every right of Allah and of His servants that they neglected, all of which has been written down and recorded against them. ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾. ﴿And﴾ after this evil reckoning, ﴿their refuge is Hell﴾, which gathers every kind of punishment: severe hunger, painful thirst, the blazing fire, the zaqqum, the zamharir, the dari', and all the categories of punishment that Allah has mentioned. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾; that is, the abode and dwelling place of them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 13, verse 19–24:

{19 – 20} He, exalted is He, says, distinguishing between the people of knowledge and action and their opposites: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [He who knows it] understands it and acts upon it. ﴿Like one who is blind﴾: one who knows neither the truth nor acts upon it. The difference between them is like the difference between the heaven and the earth. It is therefore fitting for the servant to reflect and contemplate which of the two groups is better in condition and finer in outcome, so that he prefers its path and follows its company. But not everyone remembers what benefits and harms him. ﴿Only people of understanding remember﴾: that is, those of sound intellect and complete judgment, who are the core of the world and the elite of the children of Adam. If you ask about their description, you will find no better description than God's description of them in His words: ﴿Those who fulfil the covenant of God﴾: the covenant He made with them and that which they pledged to Him, namely, upholding His rights completely and fully. Fulfilling it means giving it its due in completing it and sincerely performing it. And among the completeness of fulfilling it is that ﴿they do not break the compact﴾: that is, the pact they made with God. This includes all covenants, pledges, oaths and vows that servants make. A servant will not be among the people of understanding, for whom there is great reward, except by fulfilling them completely and not breaking or diminishing them.

{21} ﴿And those who join what God has commanded to be joined﴾: This is general to everything God has commanded to be joined, such as faith in Him and His Messenger, love for Him and love for His Messenger, submission to worship Him alone without partner, and obedience to His Messenger. They also join their fathers and mothers by being dutiful to them in word and deed and not disobeying them. They join the relatives and kin by doing good to them in word and deed. They join what is between them and their spouses, companions and slaves by fulfilling their rights completely and fully, both religious and worldly. The cause that makes the servant join what God has commanded to be joined is the fear of God and dread of the Day of Reckoning. Therefore He said: ﴿and they fear their Lord﴾: that is, they dread Him. Their fear of Him and of meeting Him on the Day of Reckoning prevents them from daring to commit the disobedience of God or falling short in anything God has commanded, out of fear of punishment and hope for reward.

{22} ﴿And those who patiently persevere﴾: in obeying what is commanded, in abstaining from and staying away from what is forbidden, and in enduring God's painful decrees without displeasure. But this patience must be ﴿seeking the countenance of their Lord﴾: not for any other corrupt aims or purposes. This is the beneficial patience by which the servant restrains himself seeking the pleasure of his Lord and hoping for nearness to Him and favour with His reward. It is the patience that is among the distinguishing qualities of the people of faith. As for common patience whose aim is mere endurance and whose end is boasting, this issues from the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, and so it is not truly praiseworthy. ﴿And establish prayer﴾: with its pillars, conditions and perfecting elements, outwardly and inwardly. ﴿And spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾: this includes obligatory expenditures such as zakat and expiations, and recommended expenditures, and that they spend wherever need calls for spending, secretly and openly. ﴿And they repel evil with good﴾: that is, whoever wrongs them by word or deed, they do not repay him in kind, but rather respond with kindness to him. They give to whoever deprives them, pardon whoever wrongs them, join whoever cuts them off, and do good to whoever harms them. If they respond to the wrongdoer with kindness, then what do you think of others who are not wrongdoers? ﴿Those﴾: whose noble qualities and beautiful virtues have been described: ﴿for them is the good outcome of the abode.﴾

{23 – 24} He explains it with His words: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾: that is, a dwelling they will never leave, nor will they desire any change from it, because they see no end beyond it, due to the bliss and joy it contains, in which all aims and objectives terminate. And among the completeness of their bliss and comfort of their eyes is that ﴿they will enter them, and [so will] whoever of their fathers, spouses and offspring is righteous﴾: from the males and females, and their spouses; that is, husband or wife. Likewise the peers, counterparts, companions and loved ones, for they are among their spouses and offspring. ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾: congratulating them on safety and God's honour toward them, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾: that is, peace and greeting from God have descended upon you and been obtained by you. This includes the removal of every hated thing and the attainment of every beloved thing. ﴿For what you patiently persevered﴾: that is, your patience is what brought you to these lofty abodes and precious gardens. ﴿Excellent is the final abode﴾: It is fitting for whoever advises his own soul, and whose soul has value to him, to strive against it so that it may take a share of the qualities of the people of understanding, and so that it may attain this abode, which is the desire of souls and the joy of spirits, comprising all pleasures and delights. For the likes of this let the workers work, and for it let the competitors compete.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 13, verse 30:

{30} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {Thus have We sent you} to your people, calling them to guidance, {and there have passed away before him nations} to whom We sent Our messengers. You are not a novelty among the messengers, so that they should deny your message, nor do you speak of your own accord; rather, you recite to them the verses of Allah, which Allah revealed to you, verses that purify hearts and cause souls to grow in goodness. Yet your people disbelieve in the Most Merciful, and they did not meet His mercy and benevolence, the greatest of which is that We sent you to them as a messenger and sent down to you a Book, with acceptance and gratitude. Rather, they met it with denial and rejection. Will they not then take heed from those generations before them that denied, and how Allah seized them for their sins? {Say: He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him.} This includes both kinds of Tawhid: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the oneness of worship) and Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (the oneness of lordship). He is my Lord, who has nurtured me with His blessings since He brought me into existence, and He is my deity, {upon Him I rely} in all my affairs, and {to Him I turn in repentance}; that is, I return to Him in all my acts of worship and in all my needs.

{31} The Exalted says, explaining the excellence of the noble Qur'an over the other revealed books: {Even if there were a Qur'an} among the divine books {by which mountains were set in motion} from their places, {or the earth was cleft asunder} to produce gardens and rivers, {or the dead were made to speak} — it would be this Qur'an. {Rather, to Allah belongs the affair entirely}: He brings the signs that His wisdom requires. So what is the matter with the deniers, that they propose such signs as they propose? Do they, or anyone else, have any share in the affair at all? {Have not those who believe despaired that, had Allah willed, He would have guided all of mankind?}: they should know that He is able to guide them all, but He does not will that; rather He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. {And the disbelievers will not cease}: in their disbelief, neither taking heed nor being admonished, {while Allah continues to send calamities upon them, striking them in their homes or landing near their dwellings, while they persist in their disbelief}, {until the promise of Allah comes}: the promised descent of the continuous punishment that cannot be averted. {Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise}: this is a threat to them and a warning of the descent of what Allah has promised them because of their disbelief, obstinacy and wrongdoing.

God Most High says to His Messenger, affirming and consoling him: {And indeed, messengers before you were mocked}. So you are not the first messenger to be denied and harmed. {Then I gave respite to those who disbelieved}, that is, to them for their messengers' sake; meaning, I granted them a period of respite until they thought they would not be punished. {Then I seized them}, with various kinds of punishment. {So how was My retribution?} It was a severe retribution and a painful punishment. Therefore, let not these people who denied you and mocked you be deceived by Our granting them respite. They have an example in those nations before them, so let them beware lest what was done to those be done to them.

{33} God, exalted is He, says: {Is then He who stands over every soul in what it has earned} — by recompense, both immediate and deferred, with justice and equity — and He is Allah, blessed and exalted; [is He] like one who is not so? For this reason He said: {And they have set up for Allah partners}. Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 13, verse 35:

{35} He, may He be exalted, says: {The likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised}: those who abandoned what Allah has forbidden them and did not fall short in what He commanded them; that is, its description and reality. {Beneath it rivers flow}: rivers of honey, rivers of wine, rivers of milk, and rivers of water that flow without a trench, watering those gardens and trees so that they bear all kinds of fruit. {Its food is perpetual, and so is its shade}: perpetual as well. {That is the final outcome of those who have been mindful of Allah}; that is, their final end and destination to which they will come. {And the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire}: How great, then, is the distance between the two groups?

{36} He, may He be exalted, says: {Those to whom We have given the Book}; that is, those upon whom We bestowed it and the knowledge of it, {rejoice in what has been sent down to you}: so they believe in it, affirm it, and rejoice in the agreement of the Books with one another and in each confirming the others. This is the condition of those among the People of the Two Books who believed. {And among the factions there are some who deny part of it}; that is, among the groups of disbelievers who band together against the truth, there are those who deny some of this Qur'an and do not affirm it. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self, and whoever goes astray, he goes astray only to its detriment. You, O Muhammad, are only a warner, calling to Allah. {Say: I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him}; that is, to devote the religion sincerely to Allah alone. {To Him I call, and to Him is my return}; that is, my return, by which I come back to Him, so that He will recompense me for what I have done of calling to His religion and carrying out what I was commanded.

{37} That is: And indeed We sent down this Qur'an and Book as {an Arabic judgment} — that is, a firm, perfected ruling, in the clearest of tongues and the most eloquent of languages, so that no doubt or confusion may befall it, and so that it be obligatory to follow it alone, not to compromise regarding it, and not to follow what opposes and contradicts it of the desires of those who have no knowledge. For this reason He threatened His Messenger — though he is protected from error (ma'sum) — so as to bestow favour upon him through his protection, and so that his community would take him as their model in the rulings. Thus He said: {And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you}: the clear knowledge that forbids you from following their desires. {You would have from Allah no protector}: one who would take charge of you so that the beloved matter would come to you. {Nor any shield}: one who would protect you from the disliked matter.

{38} That is: you are not the first messenger sent to people, so that they should find your message strange. Indeed, "We sent messengers before you and gave them wives and offspring." So let not your enemies find fault with you because you have wives and offspring, just as your fellow messengers had them. Why then do they criticize you for this, when they know that the messengers before you were likewise, except for their corrupt aims and their desires? And if they ask you for a sign of their own choosing, the matter is not in your hands at all. "It was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by God's leave." God grants permission for it only at the time He has decreed and determined. "For every term there is a Book" (ajal kitab): it cannot precede it or be delayed beyond it. Therefore their hastening of the signs or of the punishment does not oblige God to bring forward what He has written to be delayed, although He is the One who does what He wills.

{39} "God erases what He wills" of the decrees, "and establishes" whatever He wills of them. This erasure and alteration concerns other than what His knowledge has already preceded and what His pen has written, for no change or alteration occurs in that, since it is impossible for God that there be any deficiency or defect in His knowledge. For this reason He said: "And with Him is the Mother of the Book" (umm al-kitab), that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), to which all things return. It is its origin, and the other things are its branches and divisions. Change and alteration occur in the branches and divisions, such as the deeds of the day and the night which the angels record. God makes for their establishment causes and for their erasure causes, and these causes do not exceed what has been inscribed in the Preserved Tablet. Just as God made righteousness, kinship ties and kindness causes of long life and abundant provision, and made sins a cause of the loss of blessing in provision and life, and made the means of deliverance from ruin and peril a cause of safety, while exposing oneself to them is a cause of destruction, so He is the One who manages affairs according to His power and will, and what He manages of them does not contradict what He has known and written in the Preserved Tablet.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 13, verses 40–41:

{40} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): Do not hasten against them the punishment they are promised. If they persist in their rebellion and disbelief, then what they have been promised will surely befall them. Either We will show you some of it in this world, so that your eye is comforted by it, or We will take you (in death) before it befalls them, and that is no burden on you. ﴿So your duty is only to deliver the message﴾, and to make it clear to creation, ﴿and upon Us is the reckoning﴾. We will call creation to account for what they did of what was incumbent upon them and neglected, and We will reward them or punish them.

{41} Then He said, threatening those who deny: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ It has been said: this refers to the destruction of the deniers and the uprooting of the wrongdoers. It has also been said: it refers to the conquest of the lands of the polytheists and their loss of wealth and bodies. Other views have been stated as well. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that what is intended is that Allah causes the lands of these deniers to be conquered and overrun, and sends calamities upon their outskirts as a warning to them before loss overtakes them and Allah inflicts on them calamities that no one can repel. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment﴾. This includes His legislative (shar'i), decreed (qadari) and retributive (jaza'i) judgments. These judgments by which Allah judges exist in utmost wisdom and perfection, with no defect or deficiency in them, but are founded on justice, equity and praiseworthiness. No one can overturn them, and there is no way to find fault with them, unlike the judgment of others, which may or may not be correct. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾; that is, they should not seek to hasten the punishment, for everything that is coming is near.

{42} He, the Exalted, says: {And those before them had already plotted}: against their messengers and against the truth brought by the messengers. {43} {And those who disbelieve say: "You are not a messenger."}; that is: they deny you and deny what you were sent with. {Say} to them, should they demand a witness to that: {"God suffices as a witness between me and you."} His testimony is through His words, His deeds, and His affirmation. As for His words: what He revealed to His most truthful creation, by which He establishes his messengership. As for His deeds: God, exalted is He, supported His messenger and gave him a victory beyond the power of himself and his companions and followers, and this is His testimony to him through action and support. As for His affirmation: He informed His Messenger that he is a messenger, and that he commanded people to follow him; whoever follows him will have God's good pleasure and honor, and whoever does not follow him will have the Fire and wrath, and his property and blood become lawful. God affirms him in this; had he fabricated some sayings about Him, He would have hastened punishment upon him. {And whoever has knowledge of the Book}: this includes all scholars of the two People of the Book, for they bear witness to the Messenger. Whoever believes and follows the truth declares that testimony which is upon him; and whoever conceals it, God's report about him that he possesses a testimony more eloquent than his report indicates. Had he not possessed a testimony, He would have refuted his appeal to evidence; so his silence indicates that he has a concealed testimony. God only commanded that the People of the Book be called as witnesses because they are the people of this matter, and every matter is witnessed by its people and by those who know it better than others, unlike one who is alien to it, such as the unlettered Arab polytheists and others; there is no benefit in calling upon them as witnesses, due to their lack of experience and knowledge. And God knows best.
